title: A practice of looking, keeping and showing.
lede: Azola Krweqe is an artist and curator working across exhibition-making, moving image and research.
bio:
Her work begins with the material of everyday life — family photographs, public records, inherited objects — and asks how those materials shape the stories we tell about ourselves. She is interested in the archive not as a locked cabinet but as a room people keep returning to: entering it, rearranging it, leaving something behind.

Her curatorial practice is collaborative and slow. Projects are developed through conversation with artists and makers, and often take the form of an exhibition, a publication or a film. She works closely with designers to give each project its own visual language, without letting one exhibition speak for the next.

Home Affairs: The Everyday is the Archive is her current curatorial project. The full artist and maker list, programme and dates will be published as they are confirmed.

A full biography and CV are available on request.
